doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Phones, taping and 'no recording' contracts
summary: He enforces no recording, and the Yellowjackets contract has a clause.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: One thing else that I noticed, is that - last night was an example - where there is an acceptance of the audience taking pictures? And you made the comment in advance of course, flash, no flash. But there’s I guess some embracing the fact that this is here and now, we can’t avoid it, so how do we go ahead and embrace it?
Well, Wayne gets mad when I tell them to turn their stuff off, that it’s illegal. I’m very adamant about that. Buy their CDs if you want their music, you know.
Because I saw here maybe half a dozen or less that had their phone out, but they weren’t necessarily taking pictures. They were actually capturing some video elements.
Is there an understanding with them that the act that’s coming in... that that’s something that might?
Well a lot of them don’t say anything. I know in our contract with the - what’s their names - that are coming in...
Yellowjackets. They got it in their contract: Put a sign up, “No recording of any kind.” We will stop playing immediately.
So that’s what we’ll do. And I’ll announce it. And some people, they don’t know.
Yeah, that’s a tough one there. I mean it’s tough on acts.
